_what: My research-backed proposal against the current 50. Nicolas compares his gut to this and picks per row.
_backing: 7 primal movement patterns (squat, hinge, lunge, push, pull, ROTATION, GAIT) — StrengthMatters, StrongFirst, Garage Gym Reviews. Rotation is arguably the first pattern humans develop in utero, and it is entirely absent from the current 50.
rows: Nothing — no rotational movement exists in the 50
Rotation is one of the 7 primal patterns and the whole list has zero. Every movement in the 50 is sagittal-plane.
Turkish Get-Up already trains it partly · Landmine Twist
Loaded rotation plus overhead shoulder stability. We already have it in the DB from the kettlebell library.
Nothing — Plank #11 is front plank only
No frontal-plane movement in the 50 either. Side plank is the cheapest fix and we already have the whole track.
Lateral lower-body loading. Also the best hip-mobility movement that is also strength.
Split into two slots: Dead Hang (15) and Negative Pull-Up (15)
Two movements in one slot. They have different units (secs vs reps) so they cannot share one calibration row — which is exactly why the sheet got awkward.
Hollow Body Hold (30) and Hollow Rock (30)
Same problem: one is a hold in seconds, one is reps.
A track written as one slot.
Two different movements and two different loads.
Tuck Front Lever (50) with Full Front Lever as its track endpoint
A progression track, not a single movement. The track already exists in the DB.
Mark as a PROTOCOL, not a movement
It is a routine of several movements. It belongs on the list but it cannot carry reps, a calibration or a single card.
A training prescription, not an exercise. Needs duration and heart-rate fields, not reps.
Same. This is the single biggest reason 13 fundamentals 'do not exist' in the database — they are not movements.
Mark as a PROTOCOL (it is gait, at intensity)
Gait is a primal pattern, so it belongs. But it is measured in distance and time.
Keep, but mark optional and advanced-only with a caution
Loaded hip hinge to full ROM · Seated Good Morning
Loaded spinal flexion under load is genuinely contested. Worth keeping for the mobility ceiling it builds, not worth prescribing automatically.
It needs rings, which most home users do not have. At tier 50 it is fine; just be aware it gates on equipment, unlike everything else on the list.
Name it: Bodyweight Hip Hinge, with Single-Leg RDL as the tier-30 progression
The current name describes a pattern, not a movement, so nothing in the database can match it. That is why it reads as missing.
Keep both #18 and #33 but treat them as one movement at two masteries
#18 and #33 are the same exercise. That is fine, but then dead hang / negative pull-up should be treated the same way and is not. Pick one convention.
